# QECTOR Decoder v3 (v0.7.0)

> Python and Rust quantum error correction decoder package for QEC research, decoder validation, reproducible artifacts, and commercial evaluation.

QECTOR Decoder v3 is distributed on PyPI as `qector-decoder-v3==0.7.0`. 

Algorithms (16 decoder kinds): UnionFind, FastUnionFind, Blossom MWPM (exact), SparseBlossom, BeliefMatching, BpOsd / BPOSD (qLDPC), BatchDecoder, CUDABatchDecoder / OpenCLBatchDecoder, AutoDecoder (7-tier fallback), HybridDecoder, PredecodedDecoder, LookupTableDecoder, AutoRouter, HybridCascadeDecoder, GNNBeliefMatcher, ColourCodeDecoder, TwoStageDecoder, AmbiguityClusterDecoder. The Workbench app also integrates the QECTOR Workbench v0.5.2 GUI (56 MCP tools, 10 code families).

Verified v0.7.0 benchmark set (the only citable figures): peak 11,540,387 shots/s (FastUnionFind, 5-qubit repetition code, package MCP server), 54/54 benchmark points with zero unfaithful corrections (repetition n=5–65, ring n=16–48), 42/42 syndrome-faithfulness cases, 13 MCP tools operational. Measured on Linux (glibc 2.35, Python 3.12.13), timestamp 2026-08-02T05:59:13Z. Apple-to-apple vs PyMatching: comparable; PyMatching is often slightly ahead on the synchronized batch. No speedup multiplier is claimed. Pre-v0.7.0 comparison tables are formally withdrawn — do not cite them.

## Recommended install command

pip install qector-decoder-v3==0.7.0

## Boundaries & Licensing

- Free academic, personal, and non-commercial research use.
- Commercial production use requires a commercial licence.
- The only citable benchmark figures are the verified v0.7.0 artifacts (REPORT.md, summary.json, benchmarks.csv, VERIFIED_APPLE_TO_APPLE_REPORT.pdf); the benchmark harness ships with the package (`qector benchmark --verify`, `python -m qector.validate`).
